text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Airlines backpedal on move to increase domestic air fares by 200 percent following warning by aviation minister that any airline that hiked fares would be grounded.
- No fewer than 2,000 customs officers have been sacked in recent drive to root out corruption from the service.
- Experts identify the trouble with state oil company NNPC to be government policies and poor funding of the company.
- Former Nigerian head of state General Yakubu Gowon urges Nigeria and United States to meet to thrash out problems in their relations so as to improve ties.

- The manufacturers association, in its reaction to the 1997 fiscal budget announced last month, says personal income tax should have been reduced, VAT on machinery removed and clarification provided on whether loans to be granted for cottage industries will be interest free.
- Central bank mops up six billion naira from circulation through latest auction of treasury bills.
- Access Bank, a new generation bank announces plans to seek quotation on stock exchange to meet the new 500 million naira capital base requirement.

- Potential investors are shunning the distressed banks offered for sale by the central bank because of the nine-fold increase in the capitalisation required and are instead eyeing new banking licences, industry sources say.

- Diplomatic sources say Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group meeting in London on Monday will neither press for further sanctions against Nigeria nor reprieve it. Nigeria was suspended from the Commonwealth after the 1995 hanging of nine activists.
- Industry sources say Nigeria slashed its oil export to "unfriendly nations" United States and Canada last year.
- Finance minister Anthony Ani urges Nigerians with wealth abroad to repartriate their money and invest in Nigeria.
- Nigeria"s All-Share index rose by 27.67 points last week.
